dataset_family: I-CONECT (Internet-Based Conversational Engagement Clinical Trial, NCT02871921; Portland OR / Detroit MI); 68 experimental-arm participants (34 MCI / 34 NC)
method_family: Sentence-transformer (all-mpnet-base-v2) embeddings of ASR transcripts plus phrase duration, 1-layer transformer encoder over 200-sentence sequences, MLP, label-smoothing 'InfoLoss' (KL divergence); 5-fold subject-level CV
what_it_shows: The data are ASR transcripts of interviewer-led I-CONECT video chats held on study-provided devices. On 68 subjects under 5-fold CV, subject-level accuracy is 85.16% and AUC 84.75% (per fold 76.9-92.9%; test folds of 13-14 subjects). The 84.75% AUC is the best of five fold configurations; the mean over all 25 runs is 79.94% (range 74.99-84.75). Sequence-level accuracy is 72.45%. There is no external validation and no head-to-head against a specialist instrument.
why: Pourramezan Fard, Mahoor, Alsuhaibani and Dodge 2024, Computers in Biology and Medicine 176:108606. The PDF title and authors match the block content (NLP on I-CONECT video-interview transcripts, accuracy 85.16%, AUC 84.75%), and the DOI matches the map. The block has no Title/Authors fields. Read in full; the reference list is omitted from the extract. TABLE A1: PARTLY. It shows standalone detection from low-cost video-chat data with no head-to-head. It is NOT self-administered: 'semi-structured conversations via video chat with standardized interviewers' (p.6). The headline accuracy of 85.16% is just below the ~88-94% band. NARROWED WORDING: PARTLY. The design fits: low-cost data without specialist hardware, a small internally validated sample, no external validation, no specialist comparator. The best-case figure does not clearly reach 'about 88-94%'. The subject-level mean is 85.16% accuracy / 84.75% AUC (Table 3, p.8). That 84.75% is the highest of five repeated fold configurations, whose overall mean AUC is 79.94% (Table 8, p.9). Only individual 14-subject folds reach 92.85%, and per-fold values are not the per-theme or per-model means the narrowed wording counts for P-76 and P-77. INDEPENDENCE: it adds NO dataset family. It is the same I-CONECT cohort as supporters P-76 and P-77 and candidate P-9. It shares authors Mahoor and Dodge with P-76 and P-9, and Mahoor, Dodge and Alsuhaibani with P-77 (Alsuhaibani is P-77's first author). Registry stub P-11 is recorded as duplicate_of P-6 and is excluded. INTERNAL INCONSISTENCIES in the PDF: Section 4.5 calls 85.16% an AUC (it is the accuracy). Table 8's stated std of 1.93 does not match its listed values (84.75, 74.99, 78.33, 79.99, 81.66). The ablations (gamma, FC size) are reported on the same test folds, with no separate validation set described. REGISTRY/BLOCK DEFECTS: (1) The block's sample size and Sample_N_Approx '151 - 77 AD + 74 HC' are wrong. The PDF analyses 68 I-CONECT subjects (p.6-7). The 77 AD / 74 HC figure is from the related-work description of Colla et al. on the Pitt corpus (p.2). (2) The registry codes Task_Type T2, while the same MCI-vs-NC task in P-76/P-77/P-9 is coded T1, so T1-restricted filters skip it.

quotes.quote: The control group received weekly telephone check-up calls whereas the experimental group participated in semi-structured conversations via video chat with standardized interviewers on pre-selected topics.
All participants utilized user-friendly devices provided by the study to communicate with the conversational staff [16,17].
Among the 68 randomized individuals, 34 were identified with MCI, while 34 were diagnosed with NC conditions.

Since the number of available subjects in the I-CONECT dataset is 68, we assess the performance of our framework using the K-fold validation technique. We define 5 folds, and thereby, for each fold, we allocate 20% of the subjects randomly as the test set, and the remaining subjects for the training set.

the framework exhibited its lowest performance on fold 1, with accuracy and AUC values of 76.92% and 76.19%, respectively, whereas the highest performance is achieved on fold 2, where both accuracy and AUC values reached 92.85%. For folds 3, 4, and 5, both accuracy and AUC values are close to 85%. Consequently, as indicated in Table 3, the framework achieves an overall accuracy of 85.16% and an AUC of 84.75%, with the corresponding std of 5.76 and 5.97, respectively.

Table 8 shows the average AUC values for each fold configuration [...] as well as the overall average and std values for all 25 experiments. According to Table 8, the AUC values range between 74.99% and 84.75%. Likewise, the overall AUC of all 25 experiments is 79.94%, with a std value of 1.93
As Table 5 shows, the average accuracy and AUC for the sequence-level analysis are 72.45%, and 72.39%, respectively.
The Pitt corpus is used in this study after dropping subjects with only one interview which resulted in 77 AD and 74 HC (healthy control).
